# Review of iliad-137 (Iliad 21.502–611) — reviewer, passes 1 and 2

Pass 1: every grammatical label, every claim about position in the line, every cross-reference, and note against `l`/`i`.
Pass 2: Greek to `l` word by word, `l` to `i`, remembered English, house tables (Iliad and Odyssey), quotation marks and `mark`s, the neighbouring part (iliad-136 ends with Hermes’ closing “ at 21.501, so 502 is correctly a plain narrative opening), line division of `l` against `t`, whole-unit repeats (509–510, 514, 552, 562 identical to the published `l`/`i`; 544 first line identical to 16.698), and cross-references 5.373–374 (iliad-030), 5.274 (iliad-029), 16.698 (iliad-106), 11.403 and 11.407 (iliad-067), all of which check out.
`t` was not touched (verified by script: every `t`, `ln`, `v`, `p`, `mark` is byte-identical to the draft; `l` keeps the line count of `t`). `gloss.json` was not read or touched; the reviewer's pass over the glossary comes later.

Counts by finding: high 1, medium 5, low 12, plus 1 scansion sentence added (504).

| F1 | 504 | l, i, n | high | θυγατέρος ἧς was taken as a bare genitive of goal after κίε (“went back to her own daughter”). A goal needs a preposition, and the μὲν … δὲ of 504–505 sets Leto’s going against Artemis’ going to Olympus. The genitive hangs on τόξα across the verb, “her own daughter’s bows” (the same shape as Od. 19.399 παῖδα … θυγατέρος ἧς). The note stated the wrong construction as fact. | `l` “…having taken her own daughter’s bows, went back;”; `i` “She took up her own daughter’s bows and went back;”; note now says the genitive hangs on τόξα, is not a goal, and that the poet does not say where Leto goes. |
| F2 | 504 | n | scansion (flagged line) | Hand scan: ἣ μὲν τόξα λαβοῦσα πάλιν κίε θυγατέρος ἧς. Feet 1–4 are – – / – ⏑ ⏑ / – ⏑ ⏑ / – ⏑ ⏑ (ἣ μὲν · τόξα λα · βοῦσα πά · λιν κίε), which leaves θυ γα τέ ρος ἧς for feet 5–6. θυ- is short by nature but must fill the long of foot 5 (metrical lengthening), and -ρος is closed only before ϝῆς (digamma), so it is long in foot 6. The irregularity is real. | Added one sentence: “The line is metrically irregular as transmitted, at its end: scanning it needs a lengthened syllable in θυγατέρος (fifth foot) and the old digamma of ἧς to make the syllable before it long (sixth foot).” (Same wording as the note on the identical line ending at Od. 19.399.) |

## Checked as requested

- **τρέψας (603)**: correct as noted. Nominative, so it goes with ὃ (Achilles), who is the subject of διώκετο; τόν (the false Agenor, Apollo) is the one turned toward the Scamander, and τυτθὸν ὑπεκπροθέοντα is accusative agreeing with τόν. `l` and `i` keep the Greek’s words and do not smuggle in a change of subject. διώκετο is a middle form with active sense, as the note says. No change.
- **ἐξ ἧς (513)**: correct as noted. Relative, feminine genitive after ἐξ, antecedent Ἥρη; not the possessive (contrast ἧς at 504, which is the possessive, agreeing with θυγατέρος). Position claim (Ἥρη last in 512, after πάτερ) checked. No change.
- **Ἰλήϊον (558)**: the note’s claim is hedged and true to the uncertainty (adjective from Ἴλος or Ἴλιος); “Ilian” in `l`/`i` is neutral between them. No change.

## Findings considered and refused

- **Ἴλιον “Ilium” (515, 561, 588) against “Ilios”**: published Iliad parts split exactly evenly (32 and 32); the table fixes “Ilium” only with ἱρή. No binding rule is broken; left.
- **κιχήσεσθαι “overtake” (605)**: table row 6.228 has “reach” for κιχείω, but published iliad-039 (6.341) and iliad-134 (21.263) use “overtake/overtook” for the same pursuit sense; left.
- **στυφέλιξε `i` “shoved” (512)** against the table’s `i` “drive” (1.581): “drive” does not fit a person buffeted; `l` keeps “thrust”; left.
- **ἀποέργαθε λαοῦ `i` “the people” (599)**: the army-λαοί rule (F13) would give “troops”, but a genitive singular with “troops” reads as Achilles’ own men; left.
- **`i` 596 “allowed him to win glory”** (unnamed Achilles): the note names him, and the next clause names Agenor, so no misreading; left.
- **`i` 588 “terrifying as you are”** (drops ὧδε “so”): the sense is carried; left.
- **ἀλύξαι “escape” (565)**, **θάνατον καὶ κῆρας “death and the death-fates”/“the fates of death”**: agree with the Odyssey rows (odyssey-087, -106) and Iliad table; left.
- **Οὐρανιώνων (509)**: `l`/`i` are the published iliad-030 pair, as the validator requires, although the table’s Iliad row (5.898, “the sons of Uranus”) differs; that is an inconsistency in earlier parts, not this one. Flagging for the owner: see below.
- **Quotation marks and marks**: speeches at 509, 512, 531–536, 553–570, 583–589 are opened and closed correctly; every first unit carries `mark`; 553 is a one-word unit by design. No change.
- **ἑανός, ἀμύμων, ἀγερώχων, καρχαλέοι, χαλκοβατές**: the notes already say sense unknown or disputed. No change.
- **`p` marks** at 502, 511, 514, 526, 537, 544, 571, 590 agree with the packet’s ¶ marks.

## Left for the owner

- The table’s Iliad row for Οὐρανιώνων (5.898 “the sons of Uranus”, with “the Uranians”/“the gods of heaven” listed as avoided) is contradicted by the shipped iliad-030 unit (5.373, “Uranians” / “gods of heaven”), which this part must repeat. One of the two should be reconciled in the table.
- F1 changes the construction of 504 against a natural first reading; the evidence is the μὲν … δὲ contrast and the identical line ending at Od. 19.399, not a commentary.
- Second pass on `gloss.json` still to do when it exists (θυγατέρος ἧς, ἧς at 504/513, ἄστυ “town”, ἔθελγεν, λύσσα, ἔμπλητο and the other forms touched above should be checked against these edits).
